inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 1.9 cash-flow reconciliation, 'Share-based payments' 1.7 (FY25 4.9, FY24 8.1); equity-award taxes nil. FY26 is abnormally low because the FY24 LTI grant vested nil and the expense reversed; forward SBC is modelled at 1.0% of revenue (FY22-FY25 range 0.7-1.3%).
inputs.share_count_basis: 256,293,158 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 3.2 closing balance, after 5.44m cancelled under the buy-back) plus 2,044,498 unissued performance rights (Directors' Report) = 258.3m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buy-back of $18.7m (FY26) and $74.2m (FY25) is the mechanism funding the flat count; the DRP (0.44m shares FY26) is trivial. The weighted-average diluted count of 260.87m is stale because of the in-year buy-back and is not used.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Borrowings at carrying value 374.7 (FY26 AR balance sheet; facility face value 376.3 in the net-debt table) less cash 59.8 = 314.9. Lease liabilities (41.4 = 11.3 current + 30.1 non-current) are EXCLUDED because leases are treated as an operating cost (treatment B). Deferred consideration 1.2 and the declared-but-unpaid FY26 final dividend 50.0 are carried in equity_bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD. Risk-free AUD 10y government ~4.3% (Sept 2026), equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~0.95 for a leveraged, defensive-but-disrupted professional-services mid-cap gives cost of equity ~9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.2% (FY26 net finance costs 23.9 on average borrowings ~395) = ~4.5% after 27% tax. Market weights ~70% equity (880m cap) / 30% debt (375m) -> 8.0%; rounded UP to 8.5% for size and the negative-NTA, goodwill-backed balance sheet. One WACC across all three scenarios; the ANZ share-loss, US-filing and AI risks are charged in the bear flows and its 30% weight, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. FY26 lease cash of 14.9 (12.6 principal in financing + 2.3 interest on leased assets, FY26 AR cash-flow statement and note 3.4) = 2.1% of revenue is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT excludes right-of-use depreciation (10.2).
inputs.nci_treatment: None. IPH has no material non-controlling interest in FY26; statutory NPAT 80.4 is fully attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, via the Drivers/build-dcf route. IPH is an operating professional-services company (patent and trade mark attorney firms), so the SKILL.md routing table sends it to the owner-FCF engine plus the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment, SBC-light market). The goodwill-heavy, negative-NTA balance sheet (NTA -$0.94/share) does NOT change the model: the acquired-intangible amortisation (~47.9m pre-tax, 35.7 after tax in FY26) is non-cash and not cash-tax-deductible, so it is excluded from the D&A driver entirely; cash tax is computed on EBIT before that amortisation, which is what reconciles to the 41.8m cash taxes paid (27% of unlevered pre-amortisation EBIT less interest). D&A driver (1.2% of revenue) therefore covers only PPE depreciation ex-ROU (~5.2) and software amortisation (~3.5), matched by a normalised capex of 1.2% (FY26 capex of 2.9 was abnormally low vs 7.9 FY25, 11.0 FY24). EBITDA driver is pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16 (statutory 196.5 + SBC 1.7 = 198.2, 27.9%; underlying 205.9 = 29.0%; the 6.5m of 'non-underlying' SaaS/cyber/transformation costs recur in some form every year and are treated as real cost, the 2.9 impairment as non-cash). last_fcf 134.2 = reported FCF 148.5 (OCF 151.4 - capex 2.9) - SBC 1.7 - lease principal 12.6; interest income 0.8 is NOT stripped because IPH is net-debt, not net-cash. Note that reported FCF is post-interest-paid (24.0) whereas the engine builds unlevered FCF from EBITDA, so the engine's year-1 FCF sits above last_fcf by roughly after-tax interest; FY26 OCF also carried a ~15m working-capital release (receivables +6.1, contract assets +8.0) that is not repeatable and is not carried forward. The component build calibrates FY26 unlevered owner FCF at ~132m against ~137m reconstructed from the cash-flow statement ex the WC release. Working-capital capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change): receivables plus contract assets exceed payables, so growth consumes cash. Equity bridge deducts the 50.0m FY26 final dividend paid 22 Sept 2026 (the current price is ex-dividend; that cash was in the 30 June balance) and deferred consideration 1.2. Dividend coverage: FY26 dividends 98.9 + buy-back 18.7 = 117.6 vs modelled levered owner FCF ~107 (unlevered ~125 less ~18 after-tax interest) -- the FY26 payout was cash-covered only with the WC release, so the progressive dividend is a call on future growth, consistent with the >100% statutory payout the Analysis flags.
inputs.historical_lease_note: Lease principal exact for FY24 (10.3), FY25 (10.9), FY26 (12.6); approximated at ~10m for FY21 and FY23 in the owner-FCF CAGRs below.

equity_bridge.item: FY26 final dividend declared 30 June, paid 22 Sept 2026 (price is ex-dividend)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note: 'The dividend value is $50.0m based on the shares on issue at the date of this report'

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: forward organic growth, not a historical CAGR. Revenue CAGRs (13.7%/14.6%) are acquisition-driven (Smart & Biggar, Ridout & Maybee, ROBIC, Bereskin & Parr) and unrepeatable now that management has stopped acquiring; FY26 revenue was +0.6% with a full-year B&P contribution, i.e. roughly flat to slightly negative organically in AUD (ANZ LFL -4.2%, Canada LFL +5.8%). EPS CAGR 2.6%/4.5% is the honest per-share record.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.8% and EPS 5yr CAGR 4.5% both diverge >30% from the revenue 5yr CAGR of 14.6%: roll-up revenue growth funded by equity raises (FY23, FY25) and debt did not compound per-share value at anything like the top-line rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (reported FCF - SBC - lease principal) are ABOVE reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC fell from 6.1 (FY23) to 1.7 (FY26) on a nil LTI vesting, and FY26 FCF was flattered by a ~15m working-capital release and a 2.9m capex trough. Neither the 25.1% nor the 12.8% figure is a forward growth signal; FY23 also carried the QANTM integration.

base.narrative: Organic-only, low-single-digit growth: Canada (37% of EBITDA) keeps growing mid-single-digit on referrals and B&P synergies, Asia flat, ANZ stabilises after the FY26 share loss but does not recover it. Margin edges from 28.0% to 29.0% (the FY26 underlying level) on the Griffith Hack consolidation and Canadian integration -- management's stated FY27 'operational improvements to increase margins' -- and no further. Cap 13x owner FCF because the business is structurally slow and carries AI fee-compression risk; Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% would imply 15.7x.

bull.narrative: New CEO arrests the ANZ share loss (share back toward 27-28%), US PCT filings into Australia recover from the FY26 trough, Canada compounds high-single-digit with the four firms fully integrated, trade marks and legal (29% of revenue) keep outgrowing patents, and AI tooling lifts attorney productivity so margin reaches 30.5% (above the FY25 underlying 29.3%). Tax mix shifts toward Canada/Asia. Capex runs a little higher for the AI/platform build.

bear.narrative: The FY26 ANZ share loss (29.3% -> 24.1%) continues as independents and self-filers take work, inbound US-origin filings (42% of patents) stay soft, AUD strength persists against CAD/USD, and generative-AI drafting compresses prosecution fees industry-wide so the attorney-time model loses pricing: revenue falls ~9% over four years and margin de-levers to 24% on a largely fixed people and occupancy base (lease cost rises to 2.3% of revenue). Terminal growth 0.5% and a 10x cap. The progressive dividend is cut in this path; the model does not hit the zero-TV floor.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-acquisition IPH grows organically at 1-2.5%: Canada mid-single-digit, Asia flat, ANZ stabilised but not recovered. Margin returns to the FY26 underlying 29% via the Griffith Hack consolidation and Canadian synergies. Dividend is held but coverage stays tight because levered owner FCF (~107m) sits just below the FY26 dividend-plus-buyback (117.6m) until growth lifts it.
scenario_narratives.bull: New CEO stabilises ANZ share, US filings recover, Canada compounds, trade marks/legal outgrow patents, AI lifts productivity; margin 30.5%, growth 3.5-5% for four years then tapering.
scenario_narratives.bear: ANZ erosion and soft US-origin filings persist, AI compresses attorney fees, AUD stays strong; revenue down ~9% over four years, margin 24%, dividend cut, 10x terminal cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted to 30% from the 15% house default: the ANZ patent share loss is a measured, one-year, five-point decline in the core home market, FY26 revenue was flat despite a full-year acquisition contribution, management gave no FY27 guidance, the CEO is new and from outside patent practice, and generative-AI fee compression is a structural rather than cyclical threat to a billable-time model. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (ANZ recovery, US filing rebound, AUD reversal, margin expansion above any level yet achieved). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IPH is valued as a mature, ~70%-recurring professional-services cash-flow stream on an owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, leases charged as operating cost, acquired-intangible amortisation ignored as non-cash (but not tax-deductible), net debt and the just-paid final dividend deducted. The roll-up era is over -- management has said so -- so the historical acquisition-driven revenue CAGRs are discarded in favour of organic growth judgments per region. The stock trades at ~6x EV/EBITDA and ~10x underlying EPS with an ~11% dividend yield, which prices sustained decline; the valuation question is whether the FY26 ANZ share loss is a trough or the start of a trend, and the 30% bear weight is where that uncertainty lives.
key_risks_to_valuation: Australian patent market share continues to fall from 24.1% rather than stabilising (bear axis; ANZ is 42% of EBITDA)
Inbound US-origin PCT filings (42% of patent volume) stay depressed or re-route away from IPH's jurisdictions
Generative-AI drafting compresses prosecution fees faster than productivity gains offset them
AUD strength against CAD/USD reduces the AUD value of the 58% of earnings generated outside ANZ
Dividend (~117m/yr incl. buy-back) exceeds levered owner FCF without growth; a cut would hit the yield-driven shareholder base

Negative NTA (-$0.94/share): goodwill impairment risk if Canadian or ANZ firms underperform, and the 1.8x net debt/EBITDA facility covenant (maturities Sept 2027-Dec 2028) limits flexibility in the bear path
Terminal value is capped at 13x owner FCF (base), which still implies an exit EV/EBITDA above today's ~6x -- the DCF assumes the market stops pricing terminal decline
